chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluyah (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: My uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim narrated to me, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah al-Barqi, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Muhammad ibn Imran, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:

A servant will be brought on the Day of Resurrection who has no good deed to his credit. He will be told: 'Remember or be reminded, do you have any good deed?' He will think and say: 'O my Lord, I have no good deed except that so-and-so, your believing servant, passed by me, and I asked him for water. He gave me water, I made ablution with it, and I prayed for Your sake.' He will say: 'The Lord, Blessed and Exalted, will say: I have forgiven you for My sake. Bring My servant into Paradise.'

key_terms.لِمَصْلَحَتِي: For My sake / for My benefit

ai.seo_question: How can a person enter Paradise with no good deeds recorded?
ai.summary: In al-Khisal, Shaykh al-Saduq narrates this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq to illustrate the profound impact of *sadaqah* (charity) and *shukr* (gratitude) embedded in a mundane act like giving water. The scholar highlights that the servant’s remembrance of this single deed serves as the key to divine pardon, emphasizing that in Shia tradition, sincerity (*ikhlas*) can elevate even the smallest gesture to a sufficient merit for Paradise. This narrative underscores the concept of *fadl* (divine grace) where God accepts the good deed of one believer on behalf of another, showcasing the interconnectedness of the faithful.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 1-86 Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluyih - may God be pleased with him - narrated that his uncle Muhammad ibn Abil-Qasim quoted on the authority of Ahmad ibn Aba Abdullah al-Barqy, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Imran that Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) said,

“On the Resurrection Day a servant will be brought forward who has no good deeds. He is told to try to remember if he has done any good deeds. He thinks and says, “O my Lord! I have no good deeds, but once when so and so who is one of your believing servants passed by me, I asked him for some water. He gave me water and I made ablutions with it. Then I prayed for Your sake.” Then God the Blessed the Sublime will say, “Indeed I forgave you for My sake. Take My servant to Heaven. ”
